title: Reconcile waste-hauling weight tickets with customer charges
description: Reconcile waste-hauling weight tickets with customer charges. Reconcile the operating evidence before sending questions to your accountant.
intro: A hauling job may connect a dispatch, vehicle load, scale ticket, facility charge and customer invoice. Keep those records linked before comparing costs or accepting a disputed amount. This worksheet does not determine waste classification, environmental compliance, disposal authorization or the legal accuracy of a scale. Qualified specialists must resolve those questions.

sections.title: Connect the operational references
sections.text: Record the job, vehicle, container or load reference and receiving facility ticket. Preserve timestamps and units from the original documents. If a load combines several customer pickups, record the approved allocation method and identify its limitations. Do not manufacture customer-level measured weights from an aggregate load without disclosing the allocation. Keep rejected loads and reroutes visible because they can create multiple tickets for one dispatch.

sections.title: Separate measured quantities from rates
sections.text: Record gross, tare and net weight only as shown or supported by the facility record, and verify the arithmetic. Keep the facility’s charge basis distinct from the customer’s contracted basis, which may be per lift, container, weight or another agreed unit. Ask the authorized reviewer to resolve disagreements about applicable rates or materials. A correct net-weight calculation does not automatically establish that a particular customer charge is permitted.

sections.title: Worked example: net weight and invoice components
sections.text: A hypothetical ticket shows 18,400 kilograms gross and 12,100 kilograms tare, giving 6,300 kilograms net. The facility bill uses 6.3 tonnes at an assumed 70 units per tonne, totaling 441. A separately documented 25-unit charge gives a facility total of 466. The customer invoice might follow a different agreement, so the 466 is a supported facility-cost total, not automatically the customer’s amount due.

sections.title: Investigate missing or repeated tickets
sections.text: Compare dispatched jobs with accepted facility tickets, credits and customer invoice references. Ask why one load appears twice before deleting a record; a reweigh or rejected trip may explain it. Keep environmental and safety decisions outside the general financial worksheet. IRS recordkeeping guidance supplies general source-document context. The related freight and invoice guides can support broader expense review once the load-specific quantities and charge components are reconciled. When a ticket is corrected, retain the original reference and the replacement record. Ask whether the facility also issued a financial credit or simply corrected a quantity. That distinction prevents staff from assuming that an amended measurement automatically changed the payable balance.

checklist: Dispatch, load and facility ticket references linked
Gross minus tare checked in consistent units
Facility and customer rate bases kept separate
Reweighs, rejections and duplicate-looking tickets explained
questions: Does this ticket belong to the dispatched load?
Is the rate applied to kilograms, tonnes or another unit?
What supports any allocation across multiple customers?

title: Track supplier refunds through customer remittance
description: Track supplier refunds through customer remittance. Reconcile the operating evidence before sending questions to your accountant.
intro: A travel supplier’s refund notice, money received by an agency and money remitted to a customer can occur on different dates. A tracker should explain each stage without implying that a supplier message means cash has arrived. This guide does not determine cancellation rights, statutory refund obligations or who is entitled to retain a fee.

sections.title: Preserve the booking and payment chain
sections.text: Record the booking reference, supplier, original payment route and the customer’s internal reference. Link the cancellation or change request with the actual authorization. Distinguish supplier-held funds from agency-held funds and identify split payments if present. Avoid storing payment-card details or passport information in the reconciliation worksheet. The purpose is to trace events and amounts using secure references, not duplicate sensitive travel records.

sections.title: Separate approval, receipt and onward payment
sections.text: Record the supplier’s stated refund amount, any explanation of adjustments, the receipt date and the customer remittance evidence. Keep a credit voucher separate from a cash refund. An approved refund may remain outstanding, and money received may still need allocation across travelers or payment routes. Ask qualified staff to interpret the terms and legal obligations before deciding what should be sent or retained.

sections.title: Worked example: a partial cash bridge
sections.text: A hypothetical supplier approves a 1,200-unit refund. The agency receives 900 and records 300 still outstanding. Of the 900 received, 800 has been remitted to the customer and 100 awaits an authorized allocation decision. The bridge is 1,200 equals 800 remitted plus 100 held pending decision plus 300 not yet received. It does not establish that the agency is entitled to retain the 100, or that the supplier’s approved amount satisfies every obligation.

sections.title: Review aged items without inventing entitlement
sections.text: Separate supplier follow-up from internal remittance follow-up so the right team owns each open balance. Preserve corrections and subsequent receipts under the same booking reference. Have accounting review cash classification and any liability balance. IRS guidance supplies general transaction-support context, not travel-refund rules. The related credit-memo and customer-deposit guides address adjacent financial questions, while this tracker keeps the supplier-to-agency-to-customer sequence clear. For group bookings, retain a documented allocation by traveler reference and payment route. The sum of allocated amounts should match the supported group total. Keep rounding differences visible and approved, rather than sending a remainder to an arbitrary traveler merely to clear the worksheet.

checklist: Booking linked to original payment route
Cash refund distinguished from supplier credit or voucher
Approved, received and remitted amounts separately reconciled
Open supplier and internal decisions assigned different owners
questions: Has the supplier’s approved amount actually arrived?
What explains received money not yet remitted?
Which entitlement or allocation questions need qualified review?
